method: The owner pasted a real Foundry resource key into Cursor IDE. Each test sent one short prompt from a new Agent chat. A request counts as 'reached' only if Foundry or the proxy recorded it. Server side: Azure Monitor metrics for each deployment plus a temporary Log Analytics diagnostic sink (RequestResponse and AzureOpenAIRequestUsage categories). Proxy side: scripts/foundry_claude_proxy.py logs every request it receives, including rejected ones. Client side: scripts/summarize_cursor_agent_log.py over Cursor's local agent-host log. UI messages are quoted as shown. Hosts, keys and ids are not published; the tunnel and the diagnostic sink were deleted afterwards.

key_validation.check: The key Cursor stored (read from its local encrypted settings) was compared on this machine with the resource's Key2; they were identical. Only the yes/no result was printed; the key itself is not recorded.
key_validation.same_key_direct_calls: 200 on the legacy Azure chat route for the GPT deployments, 200 on /openai/v1/chat/completions and /openai/v1/responses for GPT; Claude 200 on Responses and on /anthropic/v1/messages with x-api-key (key-route-probe.json)

community: F31: staff say the Azure slot needs https://<resource>.openai.azure.com and the exact deployment name; a user confirmed it worked in July 2026
F10, F35, F37: Azure slot failures reported in 2026; staff traced F35 and F37 to Cursor's request building and fixed them in July
F32: staff pointed users at a community proxy for the OpenAI override
F8: staff say Foundry OpenAI deployments, including *.cognitiveservices.azure.com endpoints, should work through the Azure slot (November 2026)

F34: a user's identical 'Network Error' was first explained by staff as a 502 on Cursor's side that fails before reaching Azure, then turned out to be a misspelled Base URL. The message does not distinguish configuration errors from Cursor-side failures
reading: With a valid key, existing deployments, both documented host forms and a proxy that answers through a public tunnel, Cursor IDE 3.30.14 on this account produced no successful request in Foundry and no request at the proxy in eight tests. Cursor's own log shows each Azure-slot turn handed to its backend, which returned resource_exhausted; test H gave the identical error for a resource name that does not exist, so the error carries no information from Azure. Wrong keys, unknown deployments and bad api-version values are invisible in Foundry metrics and logs, so an Azure-side rejection cannot be fully excluded for tests A, C, D, E and G; it can be excluded for B, F and F2, where the proxy logs every request. The field values were read back from Cursor's settings and matched the resource and deployment exactly. This does not show that the documented option is broken in general: staff and users report it working (F31, F8), a classic Azure OpenAI resource was not tested through Cursor, and the cause inside Cursor is not visible from outside. It shows that it did not work for this account, version and Foundry resource, and that Cursor's error message cannot tell you why.
